what_it_does: This paper addresses a novel challenge: designing satellite-based data centers in low Earth orbit (Space Microdatacenters, SuDC). Unlike terrestrial data centers, orbital systems face extreme cost constraints because everything must be launched into space—power is the most expensive resource (far heavier than ground systems). The authors built a cost model accounting for power, mass, hardware cost, and communication delays, then systematically explored design choices: should you use specialized accelerators or general processors? Distribute computing across many small satellites or concentrate in few large ones? How much spare computing capacity do you need? Their analysis reveals power consumption dominates the cost, followed by hardware cost and mass, guiding hardware architects toward lightweight, power-efficient processors over sheer compute throughput.
